title: AAPOR Survey Outcome Rates
text: Let’s say draw sample 13 cases. finishing fieldwork, tabulate attempts table disposition outcomes: Using table, may wish report common survey outcome rates, : Response Rate: proportion sample results interview. Cooperation Rate: proportion eligible units ever contacted result interview; package implements AAPOR’s household-level formulas. Refusal Rate: proportion sample refused participate. Contact Rate: proportion sampled cases responsible member housing unit reached; package implements AAPOR’s household-level formulas. Location Rate: proportion cases manage locate. package extension, AAPOR-defined rate, interpretation depends located cases coded. rates come number variants, definitions standardized AAPOR. outcomerate function lets calculate rates seamlessly: available evidence supports different eligibility estimates unknown categories, pass named vector. value probability case category eligible: category may omitted non-scalar e aggregate count zero (weighting, weights supplied). length-one value—including result eligibility_rate()—keeps original behavior applies every unknown category. Dispositions always come tabulated format. Survey analysts often work microdata directly, row represents sampled case. outcomerate package allows obtain rates using format well:
code: # load package library(outcomerate)  # set counts per disposition code (needs to be a named vector) freq <- c(I = 4, P = 2, R = 1, NC = 1, O = 1,           UH = 1, UR = 1, UO = 1, NE = 1)  # calculate rates, assuming 90% of unknown cases are eligible outcomerate(freq, e = eligibility_rate(freq)) #>   RR1   RR2   RR3   RR4   RR5   RR6 COOP1 COOP2 COOP3 COOP4  REF1  REF2  REF3  #> 0.333 0.500 0.342 0.513 0.444 0.667 0.500 0.750 0.571 0.857 0.083 0.085 0.111 #>  CON1  CON2  CON3  LOC1  LOC2  #> 0.667 0.684 0.889 0.750 0.769 e_by_class <- c(UH = 0.4, UR = 0.7, UO = 0.2) outcomerate(freq, e = e_by_class, rate = c("RR3", "REF2", "CON2")) #>   RR3  REF2  CON2 #> 0.388 0.097 0.777 # define a vector of dispositions x <- c("I", "P", "I", "UO", "R", "I", "NC", "I", "O", "P", "UH", "UR")  # calculate desired rates outcomerate(x, rate = c("RR2", "CON1")) #>  RR2 CON1  #> 0.50 0.67  # obtain a weighted rate using illustrative base weights w <- c(rep(1.3, 6), rep(2.5, 6)) outcomerate(x, weight = w, rate = c("RR2", "CON1")) #>  RR2w CON1w  #>  0.45  0.61

code: fmat <- outcomerate:::fmat  # Print the dimensions dimnames(fmat) #> $outcome #>  [1] "I"   "P"   "R"   "NC"  "O"   "UH"  "UR"  "UO"  "NE"  "eUH" "eUR" "eUO" #>  #> $rate #>  [1] "RR1"   "RR2"   "RR3"   "RR4"   "RR5"   "RR6"   "COOP1" "COOP2" "COOP3" #> [10] "COOP4" "REF1"  "REF2"  "REF3"  "CON1"  "CON2"  "CON3"  "LOC1"  "LOC2"  #>  #> $side #> [1] "NUM" "DEN" #>   # Say we want to know the definition of Response Rate 2, RR2. We see # below that the numerator (NUM) column is defined by the entries with a 1, # or (I + P). Likewise, the denominator (DEN) is defined as # (I + P + R + NC + O + UH + UR + UO) fmat[, "RR2", ] #>        side #> outcome NUM DEN #>     I     1   1 #>     P     1   1 #>     R     0   1 #>     NC    0   1 #>     O     0   1 #>     UH    0   1 #>     UR    0   1 #>     UO    0   1 #>     NE    0   0 #>     eUH   0   0 #>     eUR   0   0 #>     eUO   0   0   # To use linear algebra, we define a zero-one numerator matrix 'N' # and a zero-one denominator matrix 'D'. Our count of disposition codes # is given here manually as 'x' (in the same order as N and D). N = fmat[ , , 1] D = fmat[ , , 2] x <- c(I = 5, P = 2, R = 1, NC = 7, O = 3,       UH = 4, UR = 2, UO = 8, NE = 1,       eUH = 3, eUR = 1.5, eUO = 6)  # Return all rates (x %*% N) / (x %*% D) #>       rate #>            RR1     RR2       RR3      RR4       RR5       RR6     COOP1 #>   [1,] 0.15625 0.21875 0.1754386 0.245614 0.2777778 0.3888889 0.4545455 #>       rate #>            COOP2 COOP3 COOP4    REF1       REF2       REF3    CON1      CON2 #>   [1,] 0.6363636 0.625 0.875 0.03125 0.03508772 0.05555556 0.34375 0.3859649 #>       rate #>             CON3   LOC1      LOC2 #>   [1,] 0.6111111 0.5625 0.6315789   # The same thing can be achieved with the apply family of functions numden <- apply(x * fmat, 2:3, sum) numden[, 1] / numden[, 2] #>        RR1        RR2        RR3        RR4        RR5        RR6      COOP1  #> 0.15625000 0.21875000 0.17543860 0.24561404 0.27777778 0.38888889 0.45454545  #>      COOP2      COOP3      COOP4       REF1       REF2       REF3       CON1  #> 0.63636364 0.62500000 0.87500000 0.03125000 0.03508772 0.05555556 0.34375000  #>       CON2       CON3       LOC1       LOC2  #> 0.38596491 0.61111111 0.56250000 0.63157895

title: AAPOR Survey Outcome Rates — outcomerate
text: Survey public opinion research often categorizes interview attempts survey according set outcome codes follows:  = Complete interview P  = Partial interview R  = Refusal break-NC = Non-contact O  = eligible non-interview (2.30, 2.90) UH = Unknown household/occupied housing unit (3.10) UR = Unknown sampled unit eligible/housing unit contains eligible respondent (3.20) UO = Unknown, (3.90) NE = eligible (4.0) UR 10th-edition aggregate symbol 3.20, 9th edition included UO. Legacy UO inputs remain supported. scalar e, moving 3.20 case UO UR alter rate. category-specific estimates can, new 3.20 cases coded UR standards conformance. high-level classes used calculate outcome rates provide measure quality fieldwork. outcome rates defined follows: formulas show traditional scalar form e(UH + UR + UO). e supplied category, term evaluated e["UH"] * UH + e["UR"] * UR + e["UO"] * UO. value conditional probability case unknown category ultimately eligible survey, following companion guidance (Amaya et al. 2025) . Calculate e separately frame. One vector applies cases one call; combining frames requires scientifically justified aggregation. design components, modes, phases may also require separate estimates mechanisms differ. Document scientific basis every estimate. AAPOR Response Rate proportion sampled cases yield complete partial interview, depending selected definition. RR1 = / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + (UH + UR + UO)) RR2 = (+ P) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + (UH + UR + UO)) RR3 = / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + e(UH + UR + UO)) RR4 = (+ P) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + e(UH + UR + UO)) RR5 = / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O)) RR6 = (+ P) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O)) RR5 RR6 appropriate unknown cases eligible cases unknown eligibility. AAPOR Cooperation Rates proportion interviewed cases among eligible units ever contacted. printed formulas AAPOR's household-level rates. COOP1 = / ((+ P) + R + O) COOP2 = (+ P) / ((+ P) + R + O) COOP3 = / ((+ P) + R) COOP4 = (+ P) / ((+ P) + R) AAPOR Refusal Rates proportion sample refuses participate survey. REF1 = R / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + (UH + UR + UO)) REF2 = R / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + e(UH + UR + UO)) REF3 = R / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O)) RR5 RR6, excluding unknown cases REF3 must justified study's actual eligibility situation. AAPOR Contact Rates proportion cases responsible member housing unit reached. printed formulas AAPOR's household-level rates. CON1 = ((+ P) + (R + O)) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + (UH + UR + UO)) CON2 = ((+ P) + (R + O)) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + e(UH + UR + UO)) CON3 = ((+ P) + (R + O)) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O)) Location Rate proportion cases located interview. location rate defined AAPOR's Standards, can found (Valliant et al. 2013) . Note: depending located cases encoded, may may correct formula. LOC1 = ((+ P) + (R + O + NC)) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + (UH + UR + UO)) LOC2 = ((+ P) + (R + O + NC)) / ((+ P) + (R + NC + O) + e(UH + UR + UO))

UO = Unknown, other (3.90) # NE = Not eligible (4.0) x <- c("I", "P", "I", "NC", "UH", "I", "R", "NE",       "UR", "UO", "I", "O", "P", "I")  # calculate all rates elr <- eligibility_rate(x) outcomerate(x, e = elr) #>        RR1        RR2        RR3        RR4        RR5        RR6      COOP1  #> 0.38461538 0.53846154 0.39285714 0.55000000 0.50000000 0.70000000 0.55555556  #>      COOP2      COOP3      COOP4       REF1       REF2       REF3       CON1  #> 0.77777778 0.62500000 0.87500000 0.07692308 0.07857143 0.10000000 0.69230769  #>       CON2       CON3       LOC1       LOC2  #> 0.70714286 0.90000000 0.76923077 0.78571429   # use separate eligibility estimates for each unknown category e_by_class <- c(UH = 0.4, UR = 0.7, UO = 0.2) outcomerate(x, e = e_by_class, rate = c("RR3", "REF2", "CON2")) #>        RR3       REF2       CON2  #> 0.44247788 0.08849558 0.79646018   # return only one rate outcomerate(x, rate = "COOP1") #>     COOP1  #> 0.5555556   # calculate weighted rates using illustrative base weights w <- seq(0.5, 1.8, length.out = length(x)) outcomerate(x, e = elr, weight = w) #>       RR1w       RR2w       RR3w       RR4w       RR5w       RR6w     COOP1w  #> 0.36912752 0.52348993 0.37741734 0.53524641 0.48672566 0.69026549 0.52380952  #>     COOP2w     COOP3w     COOP4w      REF1w      REF2w      REF3w      CON1w  #> 0.74285714 0.61797753 0.87640449 0.07382550 0.07548347 0.09734513 0.70469799  #>      CON2w      CON3w      LOC1w      LOC2w  #> 0.72052402 0.92920354 0.75838926 0.77542109   # alternatively, provide input as counts freq <- c(I = 6, P = 2, NC = 3, R = 1) outcomerate(freq, e = elr) #>        RR1        RR2        RR3        RR4        RR5        RR6      COOP1  #> 0.50000000 0.66666667 0.50000000 0.66666667 0.50000000 0.66666667 0.66666667  #>      COOP2      COOP3      COOP4       REF1       REF2       REF3       CON1  #> 0.88888889 0.66666667 0.88888889 0.08333333 0.08333333 0.08333333 0.75000000  #>       CON2       CON3       LOC1       LOC2  #> 0.75000000 0.75000000 1.00000000 1.00000000

title: outcomerate 1.1.0
text: Updated outcome-rate formulas, documentation, bibliography AAPOR Standard Definitions, 10th edition (2023). Added support UR, 10th edition’s new aggregate symbol cases unknown whether sampled unit eligible housing unit contains eligible respondent (code 3.20). underlying 3.20 disposition new: 9th edition included UO. Existing UO inputs results remain supported, newly coded 3.20 cases use UR. Aligned weighted-rate guidance 10th edition: individual zero weights accepted two-phase designs, invalid -zero weight vectors rejected. Already-aggregated inputs now reject weight instead silently returning results labeled weighted. outcomerate() now accepts category-specific eligibility estimates e = c(UH = 0.4, UR = 0.7, UO = 0.2). Existing scalar e inputs retain original behavior. Aggregate disposition counts now reject duplicate names rather silently discarding later values canonical ordering. Minor updates vignettes reflect changes tidyverse. Updated legacy citation, documentation, test attribute syntax current R CRAN checks.
